deities: Jwala / Jwalamukhi (Goddess of the Flaming Mouth) - worshipped as nine eternal blue flames (Jyotis) representing Mahakali, Annapurna, Chandi, Hinglaj, Vindhyavasini, Mahalakshmi, Saraswati, Ambika and Anjana. There is NO idol - the flames themselves are the deity
festivals: Navratri melas (Chaitra/Vasant Navratri in March-April and Sharad Navratri in September-October - the biggest fairs, drawing devotees from Punjab, Haryana, UP, Delhi and beyond, with round-the-clock langar)

history.dynasty: Katoch dynasty (Raja Bhumi Chand Katoch credited with the first shrine); present Indo-Sikh style structure associated with Sikh-period patronage (Maharaja Ranjit Singh's golden parasol)
history.period: Ancient (mentioned in the Mahabharata and other scriptures); present structure largely Dogra/Sikh period
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV town 'Kangra' is wrong - the temple is at Jawalamukhi town, about 30-35 km south of Kangra. Jwala Ji is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas: Sati's tongue is believed to have fallen here, and the goddess manifests as natural eternal flames burning from fissures in the rock (attributed by science to natural-gas seepage; a 1970s government exploration reportedly found no reservoir). Legend: a cowherd discovered the flames after following his milkless cow to a divine girl who vanished in light; Raja Bhumi Chand Katoch, guided by a dream, built the first shrine; the Pandavas later renovated it (folk song 'Panjan Panjan Pandavan Tera Bhawan Banaya'). Mughal emperor Akbar, skeptical, tried to douse the flames with an iron disk and diverted water, failed, and offered a gold umbrella (chhatra) which legend says turned into an unknown metal. CONFLICTS: one source credits the temple's construction to Sikh Raja Kharak Singh, while others credit Bhumi Chand with the original and the Pandavas with renovation; the temple is also said to have been destroyed by Akbar and rebuilt by the Chamba king (single-source, superbcollections.com - verify). Maharaja Ranjit Singh installed the golden parasol and his son Sher Singh decorated the gates with silver. The complex also houses smaller shrines including Gorakh Dibbi and Chaturbhuj temples. About 102 priests are government-paid.

name: Jwala Ji Temple
town_description: Jawalamukhi is a temple town in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh, about 30-35 km south of Kangra on the Shivalik foothill ridge called Kalidhar, named after the flaming-mouth goddess enshrined here.

travel.airport: Kangra (Gaggal) Airport is the nearest airport (~50 km - verify); Chandigarh Airport is about 200 km.
travel.railway: Jwalamukhi Road is the nearest (meter-gauge) station, about 20 km; Pathankot is the nearest major railhead, about 120 km.
travel.road: On NH-303; about 30-35 km from Kangra town, 200 km from Chandigarh and 480 km from Delhi, with frequent state buses from Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and J&K.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Navratri for the grand mela (very crowded). Early mornings (6-9 AM) for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple open 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (per inheritage.foundation and Justdial). Aartis (verify times): Mangal 5:00 AM (summer)/6:00 AM (winter), Bhog 12:00 PM, Sandhya 7:00 PM (summer)/6:00 PM (winter), Shayan 9:00 PM (summer)/8:00 PM (winter). Entry free; temple trust runs a guest house.
